sections.title: Overview of key ideas
sections.moral: The proof separates exact state evolution, a uniform one-day probabilistic estimate, and a deterministic recursion for the growing lead. This separation is what makes all conditioning and all uniformity in \(p\), the coloring, and the intermediate state explicit.

sections.title: Distributional transference through a solvability tilt
Asymptotic evolution of the history classes
Politicized graphs and opinion histories
sections.moral: A vertex history is nothing more than the sequence of signed neighbor-sum inequalities that caused its opinions, with weak inequalities exactly encoding tie retention. Once the degree row into every history block is known, those inequalities reconstruct every prior opinion and determine the next split.

Proof of Theorem 5.2
sections.moral: Existence of the idealized process comes from the exact conditional-mean solve; perturbative evolution comes from its uniform linearization; the critical edge day uses the full nonlinear tilted limit. These three regimes share the same local template, which is why the early stochastic trajectory can be compared to one deterministic recursion.

sections.title: Proof of Theorem 5.4
sections.moral: A faithful perturbation is small enough that the implicit conditional-mean equations still have a unique nearby tilt. Taylor expansion of the conditioned binomial rows then shows that the local template advances the response from day \(k\) to day \(k+1\), with the required uniform remainder.

sections.title: Proof of Theorem 5.5
sections.moral: On the critical integer day the nominal linear-response scale is no longer infinitesimal, so an ordinary first-order expansion is insufficient. A nonperturbative tilted limit preserves the strict sign separation and yields a fixed positive child bias, which starts the macroscopic phase.

statements.label: thm:succinct_main_result
statements.title: the main theorem (fixed lead)
statements.groupTitle: the main theorem (fixed lead)
statements.statement: Fix a real parameter \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\) and a constant \(T>1\). For all sufficiently large \(N\in\mathbb Z\), all \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\), and all \(\tau\in[T^{-1},T]\), the following holds. Let \(V\) be a vertex set with \(|V|=N\), and let \(c:V\to\{\pm1\}\) be a coloring such that \[|c^{-1}(1)|=\lfloor N/2\rfloor+\lfloor\tau\sqrt N\rfloor.\] Sample \(G\sim\mathbb G(V,p)\), and let \(\mathfrak g=(G,c)\). If \[k=2\left\lfloor\frac1{1-\theta}\right\rfloor+3,\] then with probability \(1-o(1)\) we have \(c_k(\mathfrak g)[x]=1\) for every \(x\in V\).
statements.moral: A \(\sqrt N\)-scale initial lead is repeatedly amplified by a factor of order \(\sqrt{pN}\) until it becomes macroscopic. Jumbledness then turns that lead into unanimity, and the deterministic contraction estimate keeps shrinking the minority.

statements.title: Uniformly random initial opinions
statements.groupTitle: uniformly random initial opinions
statements.statement: Fix a real parameter \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\) and a constant \(T>1\), and let \[k=2\left\lfloor\frac1{1-\theta}\right\rfloor+3.\] For all sufficiently large \(N\in\mathbb Z\) and all \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\), the following holds. Let \(V\) be a vertex set with \(|V|=N\), let \(c:V\to\{\pm1\}\) be a uniformly random coloring, and let \(G\sim\mathbb G(V,p)\) be independent of \(c\). Then with probability \(1-o(1)\) the coloring \(c_t((G,c))\) is constant for every \(t\ge k\).
statements.moral: A random initial coloring has a centered binomial lead of order \(\sqrt N\) except on a window whose probability can be made arbitrarily small. Conditioning on the realized coloring reduces to the fixed-lead theorem, with a global color flip when the lead is negative.

statements.label: def:local-admissibility
statements.title: Local admissibility
statements.groupTitle: local admissibility (LA1)–(LA9)
statements.statement: Fix \(k\ge1\), a finite set \(V\), \(p\in(0,1)\), and constants \(T>1\) and \(\phi\in(0,1/2)\). Let \(y=(\Pi,m,\eta)\in\mathcal{Y}_k(V)\), write \(N:=|V|\) and \(n[s]:=|\Pi[s]|\), and let \[\lambda\in(0,1)^{\{0,1\}^k\times\{0,1\}^k}.\] We call \(\lambda\) a tilt. It prescribes, for each block \(\Pi[s]\) and each block \(\Pi[t]\), a binomial success probability \(\lambda[s,t]\) with which the degrees from vertices of \(\Pi[s]\) into \(\Pi[t]\) will be modeled; the name refers to the fact that replacing \(p\) by a nearby \(\lambda[s,t]\) amounts to an exponential tilt of the binomial law \(\mathrm{Bin}(\cdot,p)\), and the role of the tilt is to make an independent binomial model reproduce the prescribed edge counts \(m\) after conditioning on the history constraints (condition (LA8) below). For each fixed \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\), let \(A_{s,\bullet}\) denote the \(\{0,1\}^k\)-indexed random vector with independent coordinates \[A_{s,t}\sim\mathrm{Bin}\left(n[t]-\mathbb{1}_{s=t},\lambda[s,t]\right),\qquad t\in\{0,1\}^k,\] which models the row \(\mathbf{d}[x,\bullet]\) of a vertex \(x\in\Pi[s]\). We say that \((y,\lambda)\) is \((T,\phi,p)\)-locally admissible if the following conditions hold: The regularity coordinate is true: \[\operatorname{reg}(y)=1.\] The current part sizes are of order \(N\), and the imbalances tested on earlier days are controlled: \[n[s]\ge T^{-1}N\] for every \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\), and \[\left|\sum_{t\in\{0,1\}^k}(-1)^{t[r-1]}n[t]\right|\le T\frac{N}{\sqrt{pN}}\] for every \(1\le r\le k-1\). The current edge counts have the expected scale: \[\left|m[s,t]-pn[s]n[t]\right|\le T\frac{N^2p}{\sqrt{pN}}\] for all \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\). The edge-count denominators are positive: \[m[s,t]>0\] for all \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\). The current edge-count imbalances are separated from their tie thresholds: \[\sum_{t\in\{0,1\}^k}(-1)^{t[r-1]}m[s,t] \ge_{s[r-1]s[r]} (-1)^{s[r]}T^{-1}\frac{N^2p}{\sqrt{pN}}\] for every \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\) and every \(1\le r\le k-1\). The tilt is controlled: \[\left|\lambda[s,t]-p\right|\le T\frac{p}{\sqrt{pN}}\] for all \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\). The conditioning event is nondegenerate: \[\mathbb{P}\left[\mathcal{I}_s(A_{s,\bullet})\right]\ge\phi\] for every \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\). The tilt solves the edge-count constraints: \[n[s]\mathbb{E}\left[A_{s,t}\mid \mathcal{I}_s(A_{s,\bullet})\right]=m[s,t]\] for all \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\). The next split is nondegenerate: \[\phi\le \mathbb{P}\left[\mathcal{J}_{sb}(A_{s,\bullet})\mid \mathcal{I}_s(A_{s,\bullet})\right] \le1-\phi\] for every \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b\in\{0,1\}\). We refer to these conditions by their labels (LA1)–(LA9) throughout.
statements.moral: Local admissibility collects exactly the quantitative facts needed by one transition: large blocks, controlled totals, separation from ties, a nearby solving tilt, and nondegenerate conditioning and splitting. Making them explicit lets the probabilistic theorem operate independently of the later notion of faithfulness.

statements.label: def:local-template
statements.title: The local template
statements.groupTitle: the local template \(n^{\rm loc},\ell^{\rm loc},m^{\rm loc}\)
statements.statement: Let \(k\ge1\), let \(n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}^{\{0,1\}^k}\), and let \(\lambda\in(0,1)^{\{0,1\}^k\times\{0,1\}^k}\). For each \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\) let \(A_{s,\bullet}=A_{s,\bullet}(n,\lambda)\) be the \(\{0,1\}^k\)-indexed random vector with independent coordinates \(A_{s,t}\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n[t]-\mathbb{1}_{s=t},\lambda[s,t])\); when \(n[t]=|\Pi[t]|\) for a coarse state \(y=(\Pi,m,\eta)\), this is the vector of Definition 3.1. Suppose that \(\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{I}_s(A_{s,\bullet})]>0\) for every \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\), and let \(m\in\mathbb{R}^{\{0,1\}^k\times\{0,1\}^k}\) satisfy \(m[s,t]\ne0\) for all \(s,t\). The local template of \((n,m,\lambda)\) is the triple \((n^{\mathrm{loc}},\ell^{\mathrm{loc}},m^{\mathrm{loc}})\) defined by \[n^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb]:=n[s]\mathbb{P}\left[\mathcal{J}_{sb}(A_{s,\bullet})\mid \mathcal{I}_s(A_{s,\bullet})\right]\] for \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b\in\{0,1\}\), \[\ell^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb,t] :=n[s]\mathbb{E}\left[A_{s,t}\mathbb{1}_{\mathcal{J}_{sb}(A_{s,\bullet})}\mid \mathcal{I}_s(A_{s,\bullet})\right]\] for \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b\in\{0,1\}\), and \[m^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb,tc] :=\frac{\ell^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb,t] \ell^{\mathrm{loc}}[tc,s]}{m[s,t]}\] for \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b,c\in\{0,1\}\). For a coarse state \(y=(\Pi,m,\eta)\) and a tilt \(\lambda\) such that \((y,\lambda)\) is \((T,\phi,p)\)-locally admissible, the local template of \((y,\lambda)\) is the local template of \(((|\Pi[s]|)_{s\in\{0,1\}^k},m,\lambda)\); conditions (LA7) and (LA4) supply the two hypotheses. The template depends on \(y\) only through the sizes \(|\Pi[s]|\) and the edge counts \(m\); stating it for arbitrary size vectors \(n\) allows the same formulas to drive the idealized process of Section 5, whose sizes are not the block sizes of any partition.
statements.moral: The template predicts child sizes from conditional split probabilities, half-edge masses from conditional first moments, and child edge counts by pairing the two half-edge masses. Its conservation identities explain why the same formulas drive both a random graph transition and the deterministic idealized recursion.

statements.label: thm:local-coarse-transition
statements.title: Local coarse transition
statements.groupTitle: local coarse transition (the one-day theorem)
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), an integer \(k\ge1\), and constants \(T>1\) and \(\phi\in(0,1/2)\). There exists a constant \(C_{3.3}=C_{3.3}(\theta,k,T,\phi)>0\) such that the following holds for all sufficiently large \(N\). Let \(V\) be a finite set with \(|V|=N\), let \[p\in\left(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta}\right),\] and let \(y=(\Pi,m,\eta)\in\mathcal{Y}_k(V)\) be \(p\)-attainable. Suppose that \((y,\lambda)\) is \((T,\phi,p)\)-locally admissible for some \[\lambda\in(0,1)^{\{0,1\}^k\times\{0,1\}^k}.\] Let \(n^{\mathrm{loc}}\), \(\ell^{\mathrm{loc}}\), and \(m^{\mathrm{loc}}\) be the local template from Definition 3.2. Let \(\mathcal{L}_{k+1}^{(p)}(y,\lambda)\subseteq\mathcal{Y}_{k+1}(V)\) be the set of all \(y'\in\mathcal{Y}_{k+1}(V)\) such that, writing \(\Pi':=\operatorname{part}(y')\) and \(m':=\operatorname{edge}(y')\), the following conditions hold: \(\Pi'\) refines \(\Pi\) one step, in the sense that \[\Pi'[s0]\sqcup \Pi'[s1] = \Pi[s]\] for every \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\). The next regularity coordinate is true: \[\operatorname{reg}(y')=1.\] The next part sizes follow the local template: \[\left||\Pi'[sb]|-n^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb]\right|\le C_{3.3}\sqrt{N}\log N\] for every \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b\in\{0,1\}\). The next edge counts follow the local template: \[\left|m'[sb,tc]-m^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb,tc]\right|\le C_{3.3} N^2p\sqrt{\frac{(pN)^{1/7}}{N}}\log N\] for every \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b,c\in\{0,1\}\). Then \[\overline K_k^{(p)}\left(y,\mathcal{L}_{k+1}^{(p)}(y,\lambda)\right)=1-o(1).\]
statements.moral: First transfer the fine degree array to independent conditioned binomial rows and prove its sizes and half-edge masses concentrate. Then resample uniform fixed-degree block-pair graphs; their edge splits and degrees concentrate, so the resulting coarse state follows the local template with uniform error.

statements.label: def:ambient-degree-arrays
statements.title: Ambient degree arrays
statements.groupTitle: ambient arrays, \(\mathsf G_{\Pi,m}\), \(\mathsf R_{\Pi,\lambda}\), conditioned rows
statements.statement: For \(\Pi\in\mathrm{Part}_k(V)\), define \[\mathcal{A}(\Pi):=\left\{\mathbf{d}\in\mathbb{Z}^{V\times\{0,1\}^k}:0\le \mathbf{d}[x,t]\le |\Pi[t]|-\mathbb{1}_{x\in\Pi[t]}\text{ for all }x\in V,\ t\in\{0,1\}^k\right\}.\] For \(\mathbf{d}\in\mathcal{A}(\Pi)\), let \(\mathcal{I}_\Pi(\mathbf{d})\) denote the assertion that \[\mathcal{I}_s(\mathbf{d}[x,\bullet])\] holds for every \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\) and every \(x\in\Pi[s]\). For \(C>0\), \(p\in(0,1)\), and \(m\in\mathcal{M}(\Pi)\), let \(\Gamma_{C,p}(\Pi,m,\mathbf{d})\) denote the assertion that, writing \(N:=|V|\), \[\frac{1}{pN^2}\sum_{x\in\Pi[s]}\left(\mathbf{d}[x,t]-\frac{m[s,t]}{|\Pi[s]|}\right)^2\le C\] for every \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\).

statements.label: def:aux-degree-laws
statements.title: Auxiliary degree-array laws
statements.groupTitle: ambient arrays, \(\mathsf G_{\Pi,m}\), \(\mathsf R_{\Pi,\lambda}\), conditioned rows
statements.statement: Fix \(\Pi\in\mathrm{Part}_k(V)\) and \(m\in\mathcal{M}(\Pi)\). The event \(m(\Pi,\delta(\Pi,G))=m\) has positive probability for \(G\sim\mathbb{G}(V,p)\), because the constraints defining \(\mathcal{M}(\Pi)\) are exactly those that make the edge counts \(m[s,s]/2\) inside \(\Pi[s]\) and \(m[s,t]\) between \(\Pi[s]\) and \(\Pi[t]\) realizable by a simple graph. Let \(\mathsf{G}_{\Pi,m}\) be the law of \(\delta(\Pi,G)\) conditioned on \[m(\Pi,\delta(\Pi,G))=m.\] We regard \(\mathsf{G}_{\Pi,m}\) as a probability measure on \(\mathcal{A}(\Pi)\), supported on \(\mathcal{D}(\Pi)\cap\{\mathbf{d}:m(\Pi,\mathbf{d})=m\}\). This law does not depend on the value of \(p\in(0,1)\). Equivalently, \(\mathsf{G}_{\Pi,m}\) is the product, over the block pairs of \(\Pi\), of the degree-array laws obtained from a uniformly random simple graph on \(\Pi[s]\) with \(m[s,s]/2\) edges for each internal block pair \(\{s,s\}\), and from a uniformly random simple bipartite graph between \(\Pi[s]\) and \(\Pi[t]\) with \(m[s,t]\) edges for each bipartite block pair \(\{s,t\}\). For \(\lambda\in(0,1)^{\{0,1\}^k\times\{0,1\}^k}\), let \(\mathsf{R}_{\Pi,\lambda}\) be the product law on \(\mathcal{A}(\Pi)\) under which, independently for each \(x\in\Pi[s]\) and each \(t\in\{0,1\}^k\), \[\mathbf{D}[x,t]\sim\mathrm{Bin}\left(|\Pi[t]|-\mathbb{1}_{s=t},\lambda[s,t]\right).\] We call \(\mathsf{R}_{\Pi,\lambda}\) the row model: under it the rows \(\mathbf{D}[x,\bullet]\) are independent, and the law of the row of \(x\in\Pi[s]\) depends only on the block index \(s\).

statements.title: Fiber law in auxiliary notation
statements.groupTitle: the fiber law in auxiliary notation
statements.statement: Let \(p\in(0,1)\) and let \(y=(\Pi,m,1)\in\mathcal{Y}_k(V)\) be \(p\)-attainable. If \(\sigma\sim\Lambda_y^{(p)}\) and \(\mathbf{D}:=\operatorname{deg}(\sigma)\), then \(\mathbf{D}\), viewed as an \(\mathcal{A}(\Pi)\)-valued random array, has law \[\mathsf{G}_{\Pi,m}\left(\cdot\mid \mathcal{I}_\Pi,\kappa_p(\Pi,\cdot)\right).\] Equivalently, for every event \(E\subseteq\mathcal{A}(\Pi)\), \[\Lambda_y^{(p)}\left(\left\{\sigma:\operatorname{deg}(\sigma)\in E\right\}\right) = \mathsf{G}_{\Pi,m}\left(E\mid \mathcal{I}_\Pi,\kappa_p(\Pi,\cdot)\right).\]
statements.sectionTitle: Ambient degree arrays and auxiliary laws
statements.moral: Conditioning the original Erdős–Rényi graph on the coarse state fixes every block-pair edge count and every history inequality. Independence of the original edges then factors the graph into uniform fixed-count block-pair laws, whose induced degree array is exactly the auxiliary graphical law with the same conditioning.

statements.label: prop:local-degree-transference
statements.title: Local degree-array transference
statements.groupTitle: local degree-array transference (old Theorem 3.1)
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), an integer \(k\ge1\), and constants \(T>1\) and \(\phi\in(0,1/2)\). There is a constant \(C_{3.8}=C_{3.8}(\theta,k,T,\phi)>0\) such that for all sufficiently large \(N\) the following holds. Let \(V\) be a finite set with \(|V|=N\), let \[p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta}),\] and let \(y=(\Pi,m,1)\in\mathcal{Y}_k(V)\) be \(p\)-attainable. Suppose that \((y,\lambda)\) is \((T,\phi,p)\)-locally admissible. Then for every event \(E\subseteq\mathcal{A}(\Pi)\), \[\Lambda_y^{(p)}\left(\sigma:\operatorname{deg}(\sigma)\notin E\right)\le e^{-N}+C_{3.8}\,\mathsf{R}_{\Pi,\lambda}\left(E^c\mid \mathcal{I}_\Pi,\ m(\Pi,\mathbf{D})=m\right).\] In particular, if \(\mathsf{R}_{\Pi,\lambda}(E\mid \mathcal{I}_\Pi,\ m(\Pi,\mathbf{D})=m)=1-o(1)\), then \(\Lambda_y^{(p)}(\sigma:\operatorname{deg}(\sigma)\in E)=1-o(1)\).
statements.sectionTitle: Local transference for a coarse fiber
statements.moral: Enumeration shows that, on second-moment-regular arrays, the graphical density differs from the independent-binomial density only by a bounded factor. The irregular remainder is controlled separately, so failure probabilities transfer after conditioning on histories and exact totals.

statements.label: prop:fiber-degree-array-estimates
statements.title: Fiber degree-array estimates
statements.groupTitle: fiber degree-array estimates (R1)–(R3)
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), an integer \(k\ge1\), and constants \(T>1\) and \(\phi\in(0,1/2)\). There exists a constant \(C_{3.9}=C_{3.9}(\theta,k,T,\phi)>0\) such that the following holds for all sufficiently large \(N\). Let \(V\) be a finite set with \(|V|=N\), let \[p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta}),\] and let \(y=(\Pi,m,1)\in\mathcal{Y}_k(V)\) be \(p\)-attainable. Suppose that \((y,\lambda)\) is \((T,\phi,p)\)-locally admissible, and let \(n^{\mathrm{loc}}\) and \(\ell^{\mathrm{loc}}\) be the local template from Definition 3.2. Sample \[(\Pi,\mathbf{d})\sim\Lambda_y^{(p)}.\] Then, with probability \(1-o(1)\), the following estimates hold simultaneously: Individual degrees are concentrated: \[\left|\mathbf{d}[x,t]-p|\Pi[t]|\right| \le \sqrt{pN}\,(\log N)^{2/3}\] for every \(x\in V\) and \(t\in\{0,1\}^k\). The next part sizes follow the local template: \[\left||W_{\mathbf{d}}[sb]|-n^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb]\right| \le C_{3.9}\sqrt N\log N\] for every \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b\in\{0,1\}\). The degree masses follow the local template: \[\left|L_{\mathbf{d}}[sb,t]-\ell^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb,t]\right| \le C_{3.9}\frac{N^2p}{\sqrt N}\log N\] for every \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b\in\{0,1\}\).
statements.sectionTitle: Degree-array concentration in a coarse fiber
statements.moral: Under the row model, independent bounded coordinates give concentration of child counts and degree masses. A polynomial lower bound for the exact-total conditioning event is enough to preserve their superpolynomial tail bounds, and transference then carries the estimates to the true fiber law.

statements.groupTitle: kernel splitting estimates (S1)–(S3)
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), an integer \(k\ge1\), and constants \(T>1\) and \(\phi\in(0,1/2)\). There exists a constant \(C_{3.10}=C_{3.10}(\theta,k,T,\phi)>0\) such that the following holds for all sufficiently large \(N\). Let \(V\) be a finite set with \(|V|=N\), let \[p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta}),\] and let \((y,\lambda)\) be \((T,\phi,p)\)-locally admissible with \(y=(\Pi,m,1)\). Let \(\mathbf{d}\in\mathcal{D}^{\mathcal I}(\Pi)\) satisfy \[m(\Pi,\mathbf{d})=m\] together with the estimates (R1) and (R2) of Proposition 3.9. Sample \[\sigma'=(\Pi',\mathbf{D}')\sim K_k((\Pi,\mathbf{d}),\cdot).\] Then, with probability \(1-o(1)\), the following hold simultaneously: The next partition is the deterministic split: \[\Pi'[sb]=W_{\mathbf{d}}[sb]\] for every \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b\in\{0,1\}\). The next degree array is regular: \(\kappa_p(\Pi',\mathbf{D}')\) holds. The next edge counts split proportionally to the degree masses: \[\left| m(\Pi',\mathbf{D}')[sb,tc] - \frac{L_{\mathbf{d}}[sb,t]L_{\mathbf{d}}[tc,s]}{m[s,t]} \right| \le C_{3.10} N^2p\sqrt{\frac{(pN)^{1/7}}{N}}\log N\] for every \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b,c\in\{0,1\}\).
statements.sectionTitle: Splitting the block-pair graphs under the kernel
statements.moral: Once a good degree array is fixed, each block-pair graph is an independent uniform graph with prescribed degrees. Fixed-degree edge concentration gives the proportional split formula, while neighborhood concentration gives next-day regularity; the internal-block convention contributes the necessary factor of two.

statements.groupTitle: the conditional covariance \(\Sigma_s\) is positive definite
statements.statement: For every \(k\ge1\) and \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\), the matrix \[\Sigma_s:=\mathrm{Cov}\left(W_{s,\bullet}\mid\mathcal{I}_s(W_{s,\bullet})\right)\in\mathbb{R}^{\{0,1\}^k\times\{0,1\}^k},\] with entries \(\Sigma_s[t,t']=\mathbb{E}[W_{s,t}W_{s,t'}\mid\mathcal{I}_s(W_{s,\bullet})]-\mathbb{E}[W_{s,t}\mid\mathcal{I}_s(W_{s,\bullet})]\,\mathbb{E}[W_{s,t'}\mid\mathcal{I}_s(W_{s,\bullet})]\), is positive definite, where \(W_{s,\bullet}\) is the day-\(k\) Gaussian row model.
statements.moral: Conditioning a nondegenerate Gaussian on a nonempty open set leaves a distribution with full-dimensional support. No nonzero linear functional can therefore have zero conditional variance, so the conditional covariance matrix is positive definite.

For \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\) let \(\beta[s,\bullet]\in\mathbb{R}^{\{0,1\}^k}\) be the unique solution of the linear system \[\label{eq:beta-defining} \sum_{t'\in\{0,1\}^k}\beta[s,t']\,\Sigma_s[t',t]=\varepsilon[t]\qquad(t\in\{0,1\}^k),\] which exists by Lemma 4.6; equivalently, the random variable \(B_s:=\sum_{t'\in\{0,1\}^k}\beta[s,t']W_{s,t'}\) satisfies \(\mathrm{Cov}(B_s,W_{s,t}\mid\mathcal{I}_s(W_{s,\bullet}))=\varepsilon[t]\) for every \(t\). statements.groupTitle: the idealized process (old Theorem B.11)
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), an integer \(D\ge1\), and \(T>1\). There is a constant \(\ell=\ell(\theta,D,T)\ge1\) such that for all sufficiently large \(N\) and all \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\) there exist, for \(1\le k\le D\), vectors \[\widetilde{n}_k\in\mathbb{Z}^{\{0,1\}^k},\qquad\widetilde{m}_k\in\mathbb{R}^{\{0,1\}^k\times\{0,1\}^k},\qquad\text{and, for }1\le k\le D-1,\qquad\widetilde{\lambda}_k\in(0,1)^{\{0,1\}^k\times\{0,1\}^k},\] written \(\widetilde{n}[s]\), \(\widetilde{m}[s,t]\), \(\widetilde{\lambda}[s,t]\) for \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\), with the following properties. (Base case.) \(\widetilde{n}[0]=\widetilde{n}[1]=\lfloor N/2\rfloor\), and \(\widetilde{m}[s,t]=p\,\widetilde{n}[s]\left(\widetilde{n}[t]-\mathbb{1}_{s=t}\right)\) for \(s,t\in\{0,1\}\). (Solvability.) For \(1\le k\le D-1\) and all \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\): \(\widetilde{n}[s]\ge1\), \(\widetilde{m}[s,t]>0\), and, writing \(\widetilde{A}_{s,\bullet}:=A_{s,\bullet}(\widetilde{n}_k,\widetilde{\lambda}_k)\) for the row vector of Definition 3.2, \[\mathbb{P}\left[\mathcal{I}_s(\widetilde{A}_{s,\bullet})\right]>0\qquad\text{and}\qquad\widetilde{n}[s]\,\mathbb{E}\left[\widetilde{A}_{s,t}\mid\mathcal{I}_s(\widetilde{A}_{s,\bullet})\right]=\widetilde{m}[s,t].\] Moreover \(\widetilde{\lambda}_k\) is the unique element of \((0,1)^{\{0,1\}^k\times\{0,1\}^k}\) with this property. (Evolution.) For \(1\le k\le D-1\), if \((\widetilde{n}^{\mathrm{loc}},\widetilde{\ell}^{\mathrm{loc}},\widetilde{m}^{\mathrm{loc}})\) denotes the local template of \((\widetilde{n}_k,\widetilde{m}_k,\widetilde{\lambda}_k)\), then for all \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b,c\in\{0,1\}\), \[\widetilde{n}[sb]=\left\lfloor\widetilde{n}^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb]\right\rfloor\qquad\text{and}\qquad\widetilde{m}[sb,tc]=\widetilde{m}^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb,tc].\] (Symmetry.) \(\widetilde{n}[\overline{s}]=\widetilde{n}[s]\), \(\widetilde{m}[\overline{s},\overline{t}]=\widetilde{m}[s,t]\), and \(\widetilde{\lambda}[\overline{s},\overline{t}]=\widetilde{\lambda}[s,t]\) for all \(s,t\). (Asymptotics.) For \(1\le k\le D\) and all \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\), \[\left|\widetilde{n}[s]-N\nu[s]\right|\le\frac{N}{\sqrt{pN}}\log^\ell N,\qquad \left|\widetilde{m}[s,t]-p\,\widetilde{n}[s]\,\widetilde{n}[t]\left(1+\frac{\mu[s,t]}{\sqrt{pN}}\right)\right|\le p\,\widetilde{n}[s]\,\widetilde{n}[t]\,\frac{\log^\ell N}{pN},\] and for \(1\le k\le D-1\), \[\left|\widetilde{\lambda}[s,t]-\Lambda_{N,p}\left(\gamma[s,t],\nu[t]\right)\right|\le\frac{\log^\ell N}{N}.\] By (i), (ii), and (iii), the family is determined by \((N,p)\); we call it the idealized process and suppress its dependence on \(N\) and \(p\).
statements.moral: At each day, the conditional-mean bijection gives the unique tilt matching the idealized edge counts, and the local template then defines the next sizes and edges. The universal Gaussian limits keep the construction admissible and force the exact bit-flip symmetry.

statements.label: def:faithful
statements.title: Faithful coarse states
statements.groupTitle: faithful coarse states \(\mathcal G^{(p)}_k(T,\delta,\tau)\)
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\) and \(T>1\), and let \(N\) be large enough that Theorem 5.2 applies with \(D=D_\theta\) and this \(T\); let \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\), let \(V\) be a set with \(|V|=N\), and let \(1\le k\le D_\theta\). For \(T'\ge1\), \(\delta>0\), and \(\tau>0\), the set \(\mathcal{G}^{(p)}_k(T',\delta,\tau)\subseteq\mathcal{Y}_k(V)\) of \((T',\delta,\tau)\)-faithful coarse states consists of the \(y=(\Pi,m,1)\in\mathcal{Y}_k(V)\) such that, writing \(n[s]:=|\Pi[s]|\), \(\displaystyle\left|n[s]-\widetilde{n}[s]-\tau\sqrt N\sqrt{pN}^{\,k-1}\varepsilon[s]\right|\le T'\sqrt N\sqrt{pN}^{\,k-1}N^{-\delta}\) for every \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\); \(\displaystyle\left|m[s,t]-\widetilde{m}[s,t]\left(1+\tau\frac{\sqrt{pN}^{\,k-1}}{\sqrt N}\left(\frac{\varepsilon[s]}{\nu[s]}+\frac{\varepsilon[t]}{\nu[t]}\right)\right)\right|\le T'\frac{\sqrt{pN}^{\,k-1}}{\sqrt N}N^{-\delta}N^2p\) for all \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\). In particular \(\operatorname{reg}(y)=1\) for every faithful state.
statements.moral: Faithfulness says the actual coarse state is the idealized state plus the predicted linear-response displacement, within errors small enough for another transition. It packages both part sizes and ordered edge counts, together with the regularity flag needed by the fiber theorem.

statements.label: thm:perturbed-evolution
statements.title: Perturbed evolution
statements.groupTitle: perturbed evolution (old Theorem B.12 + the unproved "faithful ⇒ tolerant")
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), an integer \(k\) with \(1\le k<\frac{1}{1-\theta}\), and constants \(T>1\) and \(\delta>0\). There exist constants \(T_1=T_1(\theta,k,T,\delta)\ge T\), \(\delta_1=\delta_1(\theta,k,T,\delta)>0\), and \(\phi_1=\phi_1(\theta,k,T,\delta)\in(0,1/2)\) such that for all sufficiently large \(N\), all \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\), all \(\tau\in[T^{-1},T]\), and every \(y=(\Pi,m,1)\in\mathcal{G}^{(p)}_k(T,\delta,\tau)\) with \(\Pi\in\mathrm{Part}_k(V)\), \(|V|=N\), the following hold, where \(n[s]:=|\Pi[s]|\). There is a unique tilt \(\lambda_y\in(0,1)^{\{0,1\}^k\times\{0,1\}^k}\) such that, with \(A_{s,\bullet}:=A_{s,\bullet}(n,\lambda_y)\), \[\mathbb{P}\left[\mathcal{I}_s(A_{s,\bullet})\right]>0\qquad\text{and}\qquad n[s]\,\mathbb{E}\left[A_{s,t}\mid\mathcal{I}_s(A_{s,\bullet})\right]=m[s,t]\qquad\text{for all }s,t\in\{0,1\}^k,\] and it satisfies: \((y,\lambda_y)\) is \((T_1,\phi_1,p)\)-locally admissible. For all \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\), writing \[\vartheta_y[s,t]:=\log\frac{\lambda_y[s,t]\left(n[t]-\mathbb{1}_{s=t}-p\,\widetilde{n}[t]\right)}{\left(1-\lambda_y[s,t]\right)p\,\widetilde{n}[t]} \qquad\text{and}\qquad \widetilde\vartheta[s,t]:=\log\frac{\widetilde{\lambda}[s,t]\left(\widetilde{n}[t]-\mathbb{1}_{s=t}-p\,\widetilde{n}[t]\right)}{\left(1-\widetilde{\lambda}[s,t]\right)p\,\widetilde{n}[t]},\] we have \[\left|\vartheta_y[s,t]-\widetilde\vartheta[s,t]-\tau\frac{\sqrt{pN}^{\,k-1}}{\sqrt N}\beta[s,t]\right| \le T_1\frac{\sqrt{pN}^{\,k-1}}{\sqrt N}N^{-\delta_1}.\] The local template \((n^{\mathrm{loc}},\ell^{\mathrm{loc}},m^{\mathrm{loc}})\) of \((y,\lambda_y)\) satisfies, for all \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b,c\in\{0,1\}\), \[\begin{aligned} \left|n^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb]-\widetilde{n}[sb]-\tau\sqrt N\sqrt{pN}^{\,k}\varepsilon[sb]\right|&\le T_1\sqrt N\sqrt{pN}^{\,k}N^{-\delta_1},\\ \left|m^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb,tc]-\widetilde{m}[sb,tc]\left(1+\tau\frac{\sqrt{pN}^{\,k}}{\sqrt N}\left(\frac{\varepsilon[sb]}{\nu[sb]}+\frac{\varepsilon[tc]}{\nu[tc]}\right)\right)\right|&\le T_1\frac{\sqrt{pN}^{\,k}}{\sqrt N}N^{-\delta_1}N^2p. \end{aligned}\]
statements.moral: A faithful perturbation is small enough that the implicit conditional-mean equations still have a unique nearby tilt. Taylor expansion of the conditioned binomial rows then shows that the local template advances the response from day \(k\) to day \(k+1\), with the required uniform remainder.

Written out in §E.5, Step 5.

statements.label: thm:edge-day
statements.title: The edge day
statements.groupTitle: the edge day \(\frac1{1-\theta}\in\mathbb Z\) (old Theorem B.14 + Lemmas 4.4–4.5)
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\) with \(k_0:=\frac{1}{1-\theta}\in\mathbb{Z}\), and constants \(T>1\) and \(\delta>0\). There exist constants \(T_1=T_1(\theta,T,\delta)\ge T\), \(\delta_1=\delta_1(\theta,T,\delta)>0\), \(\phi_1=\phi_1(\theta,T,\delta)\in(0,1/2)\), and \(\zeta=\zeta(\theta,T)>0\) such that for all sufficiently large \(N\), all \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\), all \(\tau\in[T^{-1},T]\), and every \(y=(\Pi,m,1)\in\mathcal{G}^{(p)}_{k_0}(T,\delta,\tau)\) with \(\Pi\in\mathrm{Part}_{k_0}(V)\), \(|V|=N\), the following hold, where \(n[s]:=|\Pi[s]|\). There is a unique tilt \(\lambda_y\) with \(\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{I}_s(A_{s,\bullet})]>0\) and \(n[s]\,\mathbb{E}[A_{s,t}\mid\mathcal{I}_s(A_{s,\bullet})]=m[s,t]\) for all \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^{k_0}\), where \(A_{s,\bullet}:=A_{s,\bullet}(n,\lambda_y)\), and it satisfies: \((y,\lambda_y)\) is \((T_1,\phi_1,p)\)-locally admissible. \(\left|\lambda_y[s,t]-\Lambda_{N,p}(\gamma[s,t],\nu[t])\right|\le\frac{p}{\sqrt{pN}}N^{-\delta_1}\) for all \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^{k_0}\). The local template of \((y,\lambda_y)\) satisfies \((-1)^b\left(n^{\mathrm{loc}}[sb]-N\nu[sb]\right)\ge\zeta N\) for all \(s\in\{0,1\}^{k_0}\) and \(b\in\{0,1\}\).
statements.moral: On the critical integer day the nominal linear-response scale is no longer infinitesimal, so an ordinary first-order expansion is insufficient. A nonperturbative tilted limit preserves the strict sign separation and yields a fixed positive child bias, which starts the macroscopic phase.

statements.label: prop:faithful-inclusion
statements.title: The local theorem preserves faithfulness
statements.groupTitle: the local theorem's output stays faithful (\(\mathcal L_{k+1}\subseteq\mathcal G_{k+1}\))
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), an integer \(k\) with \(1\le k<\frac{1}{1-\theta}\), and constants \(T>1\), \(\delta>0\); let \(T_1,\delta_1,\phi_1\) be the constants of Theorem 5.4, and put \[T_2:=2T_1,\qquad\delta_2:=\min\left\{\delta_1,\tfrac{1-\theta}{8}\right\}.\] For all sufficiently large \(N\), all \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\), all \(\tau\in[T^{-1},T]\), and every \(y\in\mathcal{G}^{(p)}_k(T,\delta,\tau)\), with \(\lambda_y\) the tilt of Theorem 5.4 and \(\mathcal{L}^{(p)}_{k+1}(y,\lambda_y)\) the set of Theorem 3.3 formed with the constant \(C_{3.3}(\theta,k,T_1,\phi_1)\), \[\mathcal{L}^{(p)}_{k+1}(y,\lambda_y)\subseteq\mathcal{G}^{(p)}_{k+1}(T_2,\delta_2,\tau).\]
statements.moral: The local theorem’s random errors are strictly smaller than the slack allowed in the next faithful window. Perturbed evolution centers the template at the correct idealized-plus-response values, so every locally good output automatically remains faithful.

statements.title: Day one
statements.groupTitle: day one is faithful (base case)
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\) and \(T>1\), and put \(\delta_0:=\frac{1-\theta}{4}\). For all sufficiently large \(N\), all \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\), and all \(\tau\in[T^{-1},T]\), the following holds. Let \(V\) be a set with \(|V|=N\), let \(c\colon V\to\{\pm1\}\) satisfy \(|c^{-1}(1)|=\lfloor N/2\rfloor+\lfloor\tau\sqrt N\rfloor\), sample \(G\sim\mathbb{G}(V,p)\), and let \(\mathfrak{g}=(G,c)\). Then \[\mathbb{P}\left[\rho_1^{(p)}\left(\sigma_1(\mathfrak{g})\right)\in\mathcal{G}^{(p)}_1(1,\delta_0,\tau)\right]=1-o(1).\]
statements.moral: At day one there are only the two initial color classes, whose sizes are fixed by the prescribed lead. Standard random-graph degree and edge-count concentration place their coarse data inside the first faithful window with probability tending to one.

callouts.text: Old base case claims \(\delta=0.49\). The day-1 edge tolerance is \(N^{3/2-\delta}p\) while Chernoff gives fluctuations \(N\sqrt p\log N\); the tolerance exceeds the fluctuation only if \(\delta<\frac{1-\theta}2\), which fails for \(\delta=0.49\) as soon as \(\theta>0.02\). statements.label: thm:faithful-trajectory
statements.title: The faithful trajectory
statements.groupTitle: the faithful trajectory (old Theorem 4.1)
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\) and \(T>1\), and let \(K_\theta:=\lceil\frac{1}{1-\theta}\rceil\), so that \(K_\theta=D_\theta\) if \(\frac1{1-\theta}\notin\mathbb{Z}\) and \(K_\theta=k_0=D_\theta-1\) otherwise. There exist constants \(T^\ast=T^\ast(\theta,T)>1\) and \(\delta^\ast=\delta^\ast(\theta,T)>0\) such that for all sufficiently large \(N\), all \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\), and all \(\tau\in[T^{-1},T]\), the following holds. Let \(V\), \(c\), \(G\), and \(\mathfrak{g}=(G,c)\) be as in Proposition 5.7. Then with probability \(1-o(1)\): \(\rho_k^{(p)}(\sigma_k(\mathfrak{g}))\in\mathcal{G}^{(p)}_k(T^\ast,\delta^\ast,\tau)\) for every \(1\le k\le K_\theta\); if \(\frac{1}{1-\theta}=k_0\in\mathbb{Z}\), then in addition \((-1)^{s[k_0]}\left(|\Pi_{k_0+1}(\mathfrak{g})[s]|-N\nu[s]\right)\ge\frac{\zeta}{2}N\) for every \(s\in\{0,1\}^{k_0+1}\), where \(\zeta=\zeta(\theta,T^\ast)\) is the constant of Theorem 5.5 for the parameters \((\theta,T^\ast,\delta^\ast)\); we arrange \(T^\ast\ge T\), so that these parameters cover the ranges of \(p\) and \(\tau\).
statements.moral: Start from the high-probability faithful day-one event and condition on each currently faithful coarse state. The uniform local transition estimate plus faithful inclusion advances the induction, and only finitely many fixed days are required.

statements.label: def:jumbled
statements.title: Jumbled graphs
statements.groupTitle: jumbledness; pseudorandomness of \(\mathbb G(V,p)\) (old Lemma 5.2)
statements.statement: Let \(G\) be a graph on \(V\), let \(p\in(0,1)\), and let \(\beta>0\). For \(U,W\subseteq V\) let \(e_G(U,W)\) be the number of pairs \((u,w)\in U\times W\) with \(uw\in E(G)\); for disjoint \(U,W\) this is the number of edges between \(U\) and \(W\), and in general \(e_G(U,W)=\sum_{u\in U}\deg^G_Wu\). The graph \(G\) is \((p,\beta)\)-jumbled if \[\left|e_G(U,W)-p|U||W|\right|\le\beta\sqrt{|U||W|}\qquad\text{for all }U,W\subseteq V .\]
statements.moral: Jumbledness gives a uniform discrepancy bound for every vertex-set pair, exactly the deterministic pseudorandomness needed in cleanup. The random graph satisfies it with high probability by the cited sparse random-graph estimate, while minimum degree is supplied by Chernoff concentration.

statements.label: lem:cklt-jumbled
statements.title: jumbledness; pseudorandomness of \(\mathbb G(V,p)\) (old Lemma 5.2)
statements.groupTitle: jumbledness; pseudorandomness of \(\mathbb G(V,p)\) (old Lemma 5.2)
statements.statement: There is an absolute constant \(C_{\mathrm{J}}>0\) such that the following holds. Fix a real parameter \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\) and a constant \(T>1\). For all sufficiently large \(N\in\mathbb{Z}\) and \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\), if \(V\) is a set with \(|V|=N\) and \(G\sim\mathbb{G}(V,p)\), then with probability \(1-o(1)\) every vertex of \(G\) has degree at least \(0.9\,pN\) and \(G\) is \(\big(p,C_{\mathrm{J}}\sqrt{pN}\big)\)-jumbled.
statements.moral: Jumbledness gives a uniform discrepancy bound for every vertex-set pair, exactly the deterministic pseudorandomness needed in cleanup. The random graph satisfies it with high probability by the cited sparse random-graph estimate, while minimum degree is supplied by Chernoff concentration.

statements.label: lem:cklt-contraction
statements.title: One day of majority dynamics on a jumbled graph
statements.groupTitle: numerical jump and contraction bounds on a jumbled graph
statements.statement: Let \(G\) be a \((p,\beta)\)-jumbled graph on a set \(V\) with \(|V|=N\ge1\), let \(c\colon V\to\{\pm1\}\) be any coloring, let \(\mathfrak{g}=(G,c)\), and let \(j\ge1\). Write \(M_i:=c_i(\mathfrak{g})^{-1}(-1)\). If \(\Delta_j(\mathfrak{g})\ge10\beta/p\), then \(|M_{j+1}|\le N/5\). If every vertex of \(G\) has degree at least \(0.9pN\) and \(|M_j|\le N/5\), then \[|M_{j+1}|\le\frac{16\beta^2}{(pN)^2}|M_j|.\]
statements.moral: A sufficiently large lead makes too many cross-opinion edges necessary for a large next minority, contradicting jumbledness; this gives the one-day jump. Once the minority is small, the same counting argument and the minimum-degree bound contract it by a fixed small factor each day.

statements.title: degree-sequence laws and the enumeration theorems (old Appendix C.1)
statements.groupTitle: degree-sequence laws and the enumeration theorems (old Appendix C.1)
statements.statement: Let \(\mathcal{D}_{n,m}^{\text{graph}}\) be the set of all sequences \(\mathbf{d}\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}^n\) such that \(\sum_i d_i = 2m\). Let \(\mathbb{P}_{G(n,m)}\) be the probability distribution on \(\mathcal{D}_{n,m}^{\text{graph}}\) given by sampling the degrees of the random graph \(G(n,m)\). Let \(\mathbb{P}_{B(n,m)}\) be the probability distribution on \(\mathcal{D}_{n,m}^{\text{graph}}\) given by sampling \(d_i\sim \mathrm{Bin}(n-1,\tfrac{1}{2})\) and conditioning on \(\sum_i d_i=2m\).
statements.moral: Uniform graphs with prescribed degrees are counted by asymptotic formulas whose exponential corrections depend on the degree deviations. The bipartite and non-bipartite versions are the external enumeration inputs from which the local graphical/binomial comparison is derived.

statements.label: def:bigraph_deg_seq
statements.title: Definition A.2
statements.groupTitle: degree-sequence laws and the enumeration theorems (old Appendix C.1)
statements.statement: Let \(\mathcal{D}_{\ell,n,m}^{\text{bigraph}}\) be the set of all sequences \(\mathbf{d}=(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})\in\{0,\ldots,n\}^\ell\times\{0,\ldots,\ell\}^n\) such that \(\sum_i s_i = \sum_j t_j = m\). Let \(\mathbb{P}_{G(\ell,n,m)}\) be the probability distribution on \(\mathcal{D}_{\ell,n,m}^{\text{bigraph}}\) given by sampling the degrees of the random bigraph \(G(\ell,n,m)\). Let \(\mathbb{P}_{B(\ell,n,m)}\) be the probability distribution on \(\mathcal{D}_{\ell,n,m}^{\text{bigraph}}\) given by sampling \(s_i\sim \mathrm{Bin}(n,\tfrac{1}{2})\) and \(t_j\sim\mathrm{Bin}(\ell,\tfrac{1}{2})\), and conditioning on \(\sum_i s_i=\sum_j t_j = m\).
statements.moral: Uniform graphs with prescribed degrees are counted by asymptotic formulas whose exponential corrections depend on the degree deviations. The bipartite and non-bipartite versions are the external enumeration inputs from which the local graphical/binomial comparison is derived.

statements.label: thm:graph_counting
statements.title: Liebenau and Wormald 2024, Theorem 1.4
statements.groupTitle: degree-sequence laws and the enumeration theorems (old Appendix C.1)
statements.statement: Let \(\mu_0>0\) be a sufficiently small constant, and let \(1/2<\alpha<3/5\). Let \(n\) and \(m\) be integers, and let \(d=2m/n\). Assume that \(\mu=\tfrac{d}{n-1}\) satisfies \(\mu\le\mu_0\), and for all fixed \(K>0\), \(\log^K n/n=o(\mu)\). Uniformly over all \(\mathbf{d}\in\mathcal{D}_{n,m}^{\text{graph}}\) with \(|d_i-d|\le d^\alpha\) for all \(i\), we have \[\mathbb{P}_{G(n,m)}(\mathbf{d}) = \mathbb{P}_{B(n,m)}(\mathbf{d})\exp\left(\frac{1}{4} - \frac{\gamma_2(\mathbf{d})^2}{4\mu^2(1-\mu)^2}\right)\left(1+O\left(\frac{\log^2 n}{\sqrt{n}} + d^{5\alpha-3}\right)\right),\] where \(\gamma_2(\mathbf{d}) = \tfrac{1}{(n-1)^2}\sum_i (d_i-d)^2\).
statements.moral: Uniform graphs with prescribed degrees are counted by asymptotic formulas whose exponential corrections depend on the degree deviations. The bipartite and non-bipartite versions are the external enumeration inputs from which the local graphical/binomial comparison is derived.

statements.label: thm:bigraph_counting
statements.title: Liebenau and Wormald 2023, Theorem 1.1, bipartite case
statements.groupTitle: degree-sequence laws and the enumeration theorems (old Appendix C.1)
statements.statement: Let \(\mu_0>0\) be a sufficiently small constant, and let \(1/2<\alpha<3/5\). Let \(\ell,n,m\) be integers such that \[\mu:=\frac{m}{n\ell}<\mu_0\text{ and }(\ell+n)^{5-5\alpha}=o(\ell n m^{3-5\alpha}),\] and for all fixed \(K>0\), \(\ell\log^K n + n\log^K\ell = o(m)\). Let \(s=m/\ell\) and \(t=m/n\). Uniformly over all \((\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})\in\mathcal{D}_{\ell,n,m}^{\text{bigraph}}\) with \(|s_i-s|\le s^\alpha\) for all \(i\) and \(|t_j-t|\le t^\alpha\) for all \(j\), we have \[\mathbb{P}_{G(\ell,n,m)}((\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})) = \mathbb{P}_{B(\ell,n,m)}((\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t}))H(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})\left(1+O\left(\frac{\log^2 \ell}{\sqrt{\ell}} + \frac{\log^2 n}{\sqrt{n}} + \min\{s,t\}^{5\alpha-5}\frac{m^2}{\ell n}\right)\right),\] where \[H(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t}) = \exp\left(-\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{\sigma^2(\mathbf{s})}{s(1-\mu)}\right)\left(1-\frac{\sigma^2(\mathbf{t})}{t(1-\mu)}\right)\right)\] where \(\sigma^2(\mathbf{s}) = \tfrac{1}{\ell}\sum_i (s_i-s)^2\) and \(\sigma^2(\mathbf{t}) = \tfrac{1}{n}\sum_j (t_j-t)^2\).
statements.moral: Uniform graphs with prescribed degrees are counted by asymptotic formulas whose exponential corrections depend on the degree deviations. The bipartite and non-bipartite versions are the external enumeration inputs from which the local graphical/binomial comparison is derived.

statements.label: lem:binomial_estimate
statements.title: binomial point probabilities (old Lemma A.1)
statements.groupTitle: binomial point probabilities (old Lemma A.1)
statements.statement: Fix a real parameter \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\) and a real constant \(T>1\). For all sufficiently large \(n\in\mathbb{Z}\) and \(p\in(T^{-1}n^{-\theta},Tn^{-\theta})\), the following is true. Select \(n'\in\mathbb{Z}\) and \(p'\in(0,1)\) such that \(|n'-n|< T\frac{n}{\sqrt{pn}}\) and \(|p'-p|< T\frac{p}{\sqrt{pn}}\). There exist real numbers \(\mathcal{N}_1\) and \(\mathcal{N}_2\) such that uniformly for \(x\in[-\sqrt{pn}\log n,\sqrt{pn}\log n]\cap(\mathbb{Z}-pn)\), we have \[\mathbb{P}[\mathrm{Bin}(n',p')=pn+x] = (1+O(p\log^2 n))\mathcal{N}_1\left(\frac{p'(n'-pn)}{(1-p')pn}\right)^x\frac{(pn)!(pn)^x}{(pn+x)!}\] and \[\mathbb{P}[\mathrm{Bin}(n',p')=pn+x] = \left(1+O(\log^3 n/\sqrt{pn})\right)\mathcal{N}_2e^{-(x-\alpha\sqrt{pn})^2/2pn}\] where \(\alpha = \sqrt{pn}\log\left(\frac{p'(n'-pn)}{(1-p')pn}\right)\). Factorials with noninteger arguments are interpreted through the Gamma function.
statements.sectionTitle: Binomial point probabilities and Gaussian approximation
statements.moral: Inside the central window, consecutive binomial masses vary slowly, so Stirling’s formula at an anchor point extends uniformly across the window. This yields both the Gaussian local approximation and the coarser positive lower bound needed later.

statements.label: thm:general_poly_calc
statements.title: Gaussian approximation of conditioned binomial moments (old Theorem A.2)
statements.groupTitle: Gaussian approximation of conditioned binomial moments (old Theorem A.2)
statements.statement: Fix a real parameter \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), a positive integer \(d\ge 1\), an integer matrix \(M\in\mathbb{Z}^{r\times d}\) with nonzero, pairwise orthogonal rows, an \(r\)-dimensional vector inequality relation \(\ge'\in\{\ge,>\}^r\), a monomial \(\rho\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\), and a real constant \(T>1\). For all sufficiently large \(n\in\mathbb{Z}\) and \(p\in(T^{-1}n^{-\theta},Tn^{-\theta})\), the following is true. Select \(\eta\in((T^{-1}n,Tn)\cap\mathbb{Z})^d\) such that \(\left\lVert M\eta\right\rVert_\infty < T\frac{n}{\sqrt{pn}}\), and select \(\alpha\in(-T,T)^d\). Then, \[\mathbb{E}[\rho(A-p\eta)\mathbf{1}_{MA\ge'0}] = \mathbb{E}[\rho(X)\mathbf{1}_{MX\ge -pM\eta}] + O(\sqrt{pn}^{\deg\rho-1}\log^{3+\deg\rho+d}n)\] where \(A_t\sim\mathrm{Bin}\left(\eta_t,\frac{\frac{p}{1-p}e^{\alpha_t/\sqrt{p\eta_t}}}{1+\frac{p}{1-p}e^{\alpha_t/\sqrt{p\eta_t}}}\right)\) are all independently sampled, and \(X_t\sim\mathcal{N}(\sqrt{p\eta_t}\alpha_t,p\eta_t)\) are all independently sampled.
statements.sectionTitle: Binomial point probabilities and Gaussian approximation
statements.moral: After centering and scaling, a fixed-dimensional product of binomials converges to the corresponding Gaussian. Uniform local estimates handle the central box, Chernoff bounds discard its complement, and finite polynomial moments pass through the conditioning events.

callouts.title: error in old paper
callouts.text: Old A.2: \(p\in(T^{-1}n^{-\theta},Tn^{\theta})\) should read \(Tn^{-\theta}\); the rows of \(M\) must be nonzero (a zero row with \(>\) makes the conditioning empty); the log exponent in the error was \(1+\deg\rho+d\) and is \(3+\deg\rho+d\) after re-deriving the proof.

statements.label: thm:tilted_expansion
statements.title: Tilted expansion
statements.groupTitle: tilted expansion (old Theorem A.4 perturbation_calculation)
statements.statement: Fix a real parameter \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), a positive integer \(d\ge 1\), a matrix \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}\), an \(r\)-dimensional vector inequality relation \(\ge'\in\{\ge,>\}^r\), a monomial \(\rho\in\mathbb{R}[x_1,\ldots,x_d]\), and a real constant \(T>1\). For all sufficiently large \(n\in\mathbb{Z}\) and \(p\in(T^{-1}n^{-\theta},Tn^{-\theta})\), the following is true. Select a reference size vector \(\widetilde{\eta}\in((T^{-1}n,Tn)\cap\mathbb{Z})^d\) and trial counts \(\widetilde{\eta}',\eta\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}^d\) such that \(\left\lVert\widetilde{\eta}'-\widetilde{\eta}\right\rVert_\infty,\left\lVert\eta-\widetilde{\eta}\right\rVert_\infty < T\frac{n}{\sqrt{pn}}\), and select \(\widetilde{q},q\in(0,1)^d\) such that \(\left\lVert\widetilde{q}-p\right\rVert_\infty, \left\lVert q-p\right\rVert_\infty< T\frac{p}{\sqrt{pn}}\) and \(\left\lVert\beta\right\rVert_\infty < \frac{T}{\sqrt{pn}\log^2n}\), where \(\beta\in\mathbb{R}^d\) is defined coordinatewise by \[\beta_t:=\log\left(\frac{\frac{q_t}{1-q_t}(\eta_t-p\widetilde{\eta}_t)}{\frac{\widetilde{q}_t}{1-\widetilde{q}_t}(\widetilde{\eta}'_t-p\widetilde{\eta}_t)}\right).\] Let \(A_t\sim\mathrm{Bin}(\eta_t,q_t)\) and \(\widetilde{A}_t\sim\mathrm{Bin}(\widetilde{\eta}'_t,\widetilde{q}_t)\) all be sampled independently. Then \[\begin{aligned} \mathbb{E}[\rho(A-p\widetilde{\eta})\mathbf{1}_{MA\ge'0}] &= \mathbb{E}\left[\rho(\widetilde{A}-p\widetilde{\eta})\mathbf{1}_{M\widetilde{A}\ge'0}\right] \\ &\quad+ \sum_{t\in[d]}\beta_t\,\mathbb{E}\left[(\widetilde{A}_t-p\widetilde{\eta}_t)\rho(\widetilde{A}-p\widetilde{\eta})\mathbf{1}_{M\widetilde{A}\ge'0}\right] \\ &\quad- \sum_{t\in[d]}\beta_t\,\mathbb{E}[\widetilde{A}_t-p\widetilde{\eta}_t]\,\mathbb{E}\left[\rho(\widetilde{A}-p\widetilde{\eta})\mathbf{1}_{M\widetilde{A}\ge' 0}\right] \\ &\quad+ O\left(\max\left\{p,\ \left\lVert\beta\right\rVert_\infty^2\,pn\log^2 n\right\}\sqrt{pn}^{\deg\rho}\log^{2+\deg\rho}n\right). \end{aligned}\]
statements.sectionTitle: Binomial point probabilities and Gaussian approximation
statements.moral: A small log-odds tilt reweights every lattice point by an exponential linear statistic. Expanding that weight to first order under the conditioned law gives the response term, while point estimates and tail bounds control the uniform remainder even when the trial vector changes.

statements.label: lem:graphical-sufficient
statements.title: Lemma A.8
statements.groupTitle: sufficient conditions for graphicality (new)
statements.statement: Let \(d_1,\ldots,d_n\) be nonnegative integers with even sum \(S\) and maximum degree \(\Delta\). If \[S\ge \Delta(\Delta+1),\] then \((d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) is graphical.
statements.moral: If all degrees stay near a common sparse mean and total correctly, the potentially sharp Erdős–Gallai and Gale–Ryser inequalities reduce to generous deterministic bounds. Those inequalities certify graphicality and bipartite graphicality without enumeration.

statements.label: lem:bipartite-graphical-sufficient
statements.title: Lemma A.9
statements.groupTitle: sufficient conditions for graphicality (new)
statements.statement: Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_\ell\) and \(b_1,\ldots,b_n\) be nonnegative integer sequences with equal sum \(M\). Let \(\Delta_L:=\max_i a_i\) and \(\Delta_R:=\max_j b_j\). If \[M\ge \Delta_L\Delta_R,\] then the pair of sequences is bipartite-graphical.
statements.moral: If all degrees stay near a common sparse mean and total correctly, the potentially sharp Erdős–Gallai and Gale–Ryser inequalities reduce to generous deterministic bounds. Those inequalities certify graphicality and bipartite graphicality without enumeration.

statements.label: lem:gamma_bound
statements.title: Lemma A.10
statements.groupTitle: \(\gamma_2\) concentration and lattice counting (old Lemmas C.5–C.6)
statements.statement: Fix a real parameter \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\) and constants \(T>1\) and \(K>0\). There exists a constant \(C_{A.10}(K)=C_{A.10}(\theta,T,K)>0\) such that, writing \(C:=C_{A.10}(K)\), for all sufficiently large \(n\in\mathbb{Z}\) and \(p\in(T^{-1}n^{-\theta},Tn^{-\theta})\) the following are true. Sample \(G\sim \mathbb{G}(n,p)\) and let \((d_1,\ldots,d_n)\) be the resulting degree sequence, with mean \(d\). Then, \[\mathbb{P}\left[\sum_{i=1}^n(d_i-d)^2\ge Cpn^2\text{ and }\max_{i\in[n]}|d_i-pn|\le pn\right]\le\exp(-Kn).\] Consider \(\ell\in\mathbb{Z}\) with \(\ell\in[T^{-1}n,Tn]\). Sample \(G\sim\mathbb{G}(\ell,n,p)\) and let \((s_1,\ldots,s_\ell),(t_1,\ldots,t_n)\) be the resulting degree sequences, with means \(s\) and \(t\) respectively. Then, \[\mathbb{P}\left[\left(\sum_{i=1}^\ell(s_i-s)^2\ge Cp\ell n\text{ or }\sum_{j=1}^n(t_j-t)^2\ge Cp\ell n\right)\text{ and }\mathcal{K}_{\ell,n}\right]\le\exp(-Kn),\] where \(\mathcal{K}_{\ell,n}\) denotes the event that \(|s_i-pn|\le pn\) for all \(i\in[\ell]\) and \(|t_j-p\ell|\le pn\) for all \(j\in[n]\).
statements.moral: Truncated binomial quadratic deviations concentrate by exponential moments. For the bounded zero-sum lattice count, choose most coordinates freely and use concentration of their sum, then reserve a block of bounded coordinates to correct that sum; a single final coordinate need not stay inside the permitted interval.

statements.label: lem:basic_counting
statements.title: Lemma A.11
statements.groupTitle: \(\gamma_2\) concentration and lattice counting (old Lemmas C.5–C.6)
statements.statement: Fix a real parameter \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\) and constants \(T>1\) and \(C>0\). There exists a constant \(C_{A.11}(C)=C_{A.11}(\theta,T,C)>0\) such that for all sufficiently large \(n\in\mathbb{Z}\) and \(p\in(T^{-1}n^{-\theta},Tn^{-\theta})\), the number of integer sequences \[\left|\left\{(y_1,\ldots,y_n)\in\left([-C\sqrt{np},C\sqrt{np}]\cap\mathbb{Z}\right)^n : y_1+\cdots+y_n = 0 \right\}\right|\] is at least \(\exp(-C_{A.11}(C)\,n)(\sqrt{np})^n\).
statements.moral: Truncated binomial quadratic deviations concentrate by exponential moments. For the bounded zero-sum lattice count, choose most coordinates freely and use concentration of their sum, then reserve a block of bounded coordinates to correct that sum; a single final coordinate need not stay inside the permitted interval.

statements.label: lem:open-conditioning
statements.title: Conditioning on an open set
statements.groupTitle: conditioning a Gaussian on an open convex set (new)
statements.statement: Let \(X\sim\mathcal{N}(\gamma,\Sigma)\) with \(\Sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\) positive definite and let \(\mathcal{O}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a nonempty open convex set. Then \(\mathbb{P}[X\in\mathcal{O}]>0\), \(\mathbb{E}[X\mid X\in\mathcal{O}]\in\mathcal{O}\), and \(\mathrm{Cov}(X\mid X\in\mathcal{O})\) is positive definite.
statements.sectionTitle: Conditioning a Gaussian vector on an open set
statements.moral: A nondegenerate Gaussian has positive density everywhere, so every nonempty open conditioning set has positive probability. If the set is convex, its conditional mean lies in its interior and the conditioned covariance remains positive definite because the support is full-dimensional.

statements.title: Automatic graphicality
statements.groupTitle: automatic graphicality (new)
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), an integer \(k\ge1\), and \(T>1\). For all sufficiently large \(N\), the following holds. Let \(V\) be a finite set with \(|V|=N\), let \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\), and let \(\Pi\in\mathrm{Part}_k(V)\) and \(m\in\mathcal{M}(\Pi)\) satisfy \[|\Pi[s]|\ge T^{-1}N\] and \[\left|m[s,t]-p|\Pi[s]||\Pi[t]|\right|\le T\frac{N^2p}{\sqrt{pN}}\] for every \(s,t\in\{0,1\}^k\). If \(\mathbf{d}\in\mathcal{A}(\Pi)\) satisfies \(m(\Pi,\mathbf{d})=m\) and \(\kappa_p(\Pi,\mathbf{d})\), then \(\mathbf{d}\in\mathcal{D}(\Pi)\).
statements.sectionTitle: Graphicality of the arrays in the fiber
statements.moral: Regular arrays in the relevant sparse window have all degrees close to their block means and satisfy the required totals. The sufficient graphicality lemmas then certify every internal and bipartite block pair, closing the support mismatch between the row law and graphical law.

statements.title: Enumeration comparison
statements.groupTitle: enumeration comparison, weak and strong (old Lemmas 3.3 and 3.2)
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), an integer \(k\ge1\), and constants \(T>1\) and \(\phi\in(0,1/2)\). There is a constant \(C_{B.2}=C_{B.2}(\theta,k,T)>0\), and for every \(C_\Gamma>0\) a constant \(C'_{B.2}(C_\Gamma)=C'_{B.2}(\theta,k,T,C_\Gamma)>1\), such that for all sufficiently large \(N\) the following holds. Let \(V\) be a finite set with \(|V|=N\), let \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\), suppose that \((y,\lambda)\) is \((T,\phi,p)\)-locally admissible with \(y=(\Pi,m,1)\), and let \(\mathbf{d}\in\mathcal{A}(\Pi)\) satisfy \(m(\Pi,\mathbf{d})=m\) and \(\kappa_p(\Pi,\mathbf{d})\). (Weak comparison.) \[\begin{aligned} \mathsf{G}_{\Pi,m}(\mathbf{d})&\le\exp\{C_{B.2}(pN)^{2/7}\}\,\mathsf{R}_{\Pi,\lambda}(\mathbf{d}\mid m(\Pi,\mathbf{D})=m),\\ \mathsf{G}_{\Pi,m}(\mathbf{d})&\ge\exp\{-C_{B.2}(pN)^{2/7}\}\,\mathsf{R}_{\Pi,\lambda}(\mathbf{d}\mid m(\Pi,\mathbf{D})=m). \end{aligned}\] (Strong comparison.) If \(\mathbf{d}\) also satisfies \(\Gamma_{C_\Gamma,p}(\Pi,m,\mathbf{d})\), then \[\begin{aligned} \mathsf{G}_{\Pi,m}(\mathbf{d})&\le C'_{B.2}(C_\Gamma)\,\mathsf{R}_{\Pi,\lambda}(\mathbf{d}\mid m(\Pi,\mathbf{D})=m),\\ \mathsf{G}_{\Pi,m}(\mathbf{d})&\ge C'_{B.2}(C_\Gamma)^{-1}\,\mathsf{R}_{\Pi,\lambda}(\mathbf{d}\mid m(\Pi,\mathbf{D})=m). \end{aligned}\]

statements.title: edge enumeration in a uniform graph with given degrees (old Lemma C.7)
statements.groupTitle: edge enumeration in a uniform graph with given degrees (old Lemma C.7)
statements.statement: Fix a real parameter \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\) and a constant \(T>1\). For all sufficiently large \(n\in\mathbb{Z}\) and \(p\in(T^{-1}n^{-\theta},Tn^{-\theta})\), the following are true. Pick a subset \(U\subset[n]\) satisfying \(|U|,n-|U|\ge T^{-1}n\). Sample \(G\) uniformly at random from all graphs with degree sequence \(\mathbf{d}\), and let \(X = |E(G[U])|\) (the number of edges in the induced subgraph on vertex set \(U\)). Then, \[\mathbb{P}\left[\left|X - \frac{\left(\sum_{x\in U}d_x\right)^2}{4m}\right| \ge n^2p\sqrt{\frac{(pn)^{1/7}}{n}}\log n\right] < \frac{1}{\log n}.\] Select \(m\in\mathbb{Z}\) satisfying \(|m-pn(n-1)/2| \le T n^2p/\sqrt{pn}\), and select \(\mathbf{d}\in\mathcal{D}_{n,m}^{\text{graph}}\) such that \(|d_i-pn|\le(pn)^{4/7}\) for all \(i\in[n]\). Pick a subset \(U\subset[n]\) satisfying \(|U|,n-|U|\ge T^{-1}n\). Sample \(G\) uniformly at random from all graphs with degree sequence \(\mathbf{d}\), and let \(X = |E(G[U,[n]\setminus U])|\) (the number of edges in the induced bipartite subgraph with vertex sets \(U\) and \([n]\setminus U\)). Then, \[\mathbb{P}\left[\left|X - \frac{\left(\sum_{x\in U}d_x\right)\left(\sum_{y\in[n]\setminus U}d_y\right)}{2m}\right| \ge n^2p\sqrt{\frac{(pn)^{1/7}}{n}}\log n\right] < \frac{1}{\log n}.\] Select \(\ell\in\mathbb{Z}\cap[T^{-1}n,Tn]\). Select \(m\in\mathbb{Z}\) satisfying \(|m-p\ell n| \le T n^2p/\sqrt{pn}\), and select \((\mathbf{s},\mathbf{t})\in\mathcal{D}_{\ell,n,m}^{\text{bigraph}}\) such that \(|s_i-pn|\le(pn)^{4/7}\) for all \(i\in[\ell]\) and \(|t_j-p\ell|\le (pn)^{4/7}\) for all \(j\in[n]\). statements.statement: Let \(d\ge1\) and let \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be open. A map \(f\colon\mathbb{R}^d\to B\) is a strong bijection if it is a bijection and both \(f\) and \(f^{-1}\colon B\to\mathbb{R}^d\) are smooth.

statements.label: lem:strong-bijection-lipschitz
statements.title: Lipschitz bounds on compact sets
statements.groupTitle: strong bijections (old Definition B.1)
statements.statement: Let \(f\colon\mathbb{R}^d\to B\) be a strong bijection and let \(K\subseteq B\) be compact. Then there is a constant \(L=L(f,K)\ge1\) such that \[L^{-1}|y-z|\le\left|f^{-1}(y)-f^{-1}(z)\right|\le L|y-z|\qquad\text{for all }y,z\in K .\]
statements.moral: A strong bijection is a smooth global coordinate change onto an open set. On compact subsets, ordinary derivative and inverse-derivative bounds automatically provide the two Lipschitz estimates needed by the perturbative applications.

statements.label: thm:orthant-bijection
statements.title: Theorem D.3
statements.groupTitle: the conditional-mean map onto an open convex set is a strong bijection (old Theorem B.2, Lemmas B.3–B.5)
statements.statement: Let \(d\ge1\), let \(\Sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\) be positive definite, and let \(\mathcal{O}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be a nonempty open convex set. For \(\gamma\in\mathbb{R}^d\) let \(X^\gamma\sim\mathcal{N}(\gamma,\Sigma)\). The map \[F_{\mathcal{O}}\colon\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathcal{O},\qquad F_{\mathcal{O}}(\gamma):=\mathbb{E}\left[X^\gamma\mid X^\gamma\in\mathcal{O}\right],\] is well defined, that is, its values lie in \(\mathcal{O}\), and it is a strong bijection. Its Jacobian at \(\gamma\) is \(\mathrm{Cov}(X^\gamma\mid X^\gamma\in\mathcal{O})\,\Sigma^{-1}\), which is invertible.
statements.moral: The conditional mean is the gradient of a smooth strictly convex log-partition function, so positive-definite conditional covariance gives local invertibility and global injectivity. For each target inside the conditioning set, an interior ball makes the corresponding convex dual coercive; its minimizer maps exactly to that target, giving surjectivity without any boundary-at-infinity analysis.

statements.label: cor:cone-bijection
statements.title: Conditional means on a cone
statements.groupTitle: the cone case \(\{Mx>0\}\), \(0\le r\le d\)
statements.statement: Let \(d\ge1\), let \(0\le r\le d\), let \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}\) have rank \(r\), and let \(\Sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\) be positive definite. Let \(\mathcal{C}_M:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:Mx>0\}\), where \(Mx>0\) means that every coordinate is positive, so that \(\mathcal{C}_M=\mathbb{R}^d\) when \(r=0\). Then \(\mathcal{C}_M\) is a nonempty open convex set, and the map \(F_{\mathcal{C}_M}\) of Theorem D.3 is a strong bijection \(\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathcal{C}_M\).
statements.moral: A full-row-rank system \(Mx>0\) defines a nonempty open convex cone with exactly the lower-dimensional collection of history constraints needed in the paper. Applying the general conditional-mean bijection to this set fixes the old full-orthant mismatch.

statements.label: thm:perturbed-bijection
statements.title: Perturbation of a strong bijection
statements.groupTitle: perturbation of a strong bijection (old Theorem B.6 homotopy_ivt)
statements.statement: Let \(d\ge1\), let \(B\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be open, let \(f\colon\mathbb{R}^d\to B\) be a strong bijection, let \(\mathcal{K}\subseteq B\) be compact, and let \(C_0>0\). Put \(R_0:=\max_{y\in\mathcal{K}}|f^{-1}(y)|+1\) when \(\mathcal{K}\ne\emptyset\), and \(R_0:=1\) when \(\mathcal{K}=\emptyset\). There exist \(\varepsilon_0>0\) and \(C>0\), depending only on \(f\), \(\mathcal{K}\), and \(C_0\), such that the following holds. Let \(0<\varepsilon<\varepsilon_0\) and let \(g\colon\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^d\) be a continuous map with \[\sup_{|x|\le R_0}\left|g(x)-f(x)\right|\le C_0\,\varepsilon .\] Then for every \(y\in\mathcal{K}\) there is \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\) with \[g(x)=y\qquad\text{and}\qquad\left|x-f^{-1}(y)\right|\le C\varepsilon .\] In particular this applies to \(B=\mathcal{C}_M\) as in Corollary D.4 and, for \(T>1\), to the compact set \[\mathcal{K}_T:=\left\{y\in\mathcal{C}_M:\left\lVert y\right\rVert_\infty\le T\text{ and }\min_{1\le i\le r}(My)_i\ge T^{-1}\right\}\] (the closed cube \([-T,T]^d\) when \(r=0\)), with \(R_0\), \(\varepsilon_0\), and \(C\) depending only on \(d\), \(M\), \(f\), \(C_0\), and \(T\).
statements.moral: On a compact target set, composing a small perturbation with the inverse gives a map close to the identity. Brouwer supplies a preimage, and the inverse Lipschitz estimate places the constructed preimage near the unperturbed solution. This theorem does not assert uniqueness; tilt uniqueness comes separately from full affine support and strict convexity in Lemma E.1.

callouts.title: error in old paper
callouts.text: Old B.6 hypothesis "\(\|My\|_\infty\ge T^{-1}\)" bounds one coordinate of \(My\) from below, not all of them; the proof needs \(\min_i(My)_i\ge T^{-1}\) (distance from the boundary of the cone). Also its contraction homotopy ends at "\(f(0)\)" where \(f_\ve(0)\) is meant, and the degree-theory step ("cannot be null-homotopic") is asserted without a reference; \(r=0\) (a linear \(f_s\) onto \(\mb R^d\), needed in B.12) is not covered by "\(\{Mx>0\}\)". All moot in the Brouwer proof.

statements.label: lem:tilt-uniqueness
statements.title: The conditioned mean map is injective
statements.groupTitle: uniqueness of tilts (conditioned exponential family)
statements.statement: Let \(d\ge1\), let \(\eta\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}^d\), let \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}\), and let \(\ge'\in\{\ge,>\}^r\). Suppose that the set \(S:=\{a\in\prod_{t\in[d]}\{0,\ldots,\eta_t\}:Ma\ge'0\}\) is not contained in an affine hyperplane of \(\mathbb{R}^d\). For \(q\in(0,1)^d\) let \(A^q\) have independent coordinates \(A^q_t\sim\mathrm{Bin}(\eta_t,q_t)\). Then \(\mathbb{P}[MA^q\ge'0]>0\) for every \(q\), and the map \[(0,1)^d\to\mathbb{R}^d,\qquad q\mapsto\mathbb{E}\left[A^q\mid MA^q\ge'0\right],\] is injective.
statements.moral: Two tilts with the same conditioned mean have zero expected pairing between their probability difference and log-likelihood-ratio difference. Every summand is nonnegative, so full affine support forces the likelihood ratio to be constant and hence the tilt parameters to agree.

statements.label: lem:gaussian-regularity
statements.title: Regularity of Gaussian functionals
statements.groupTitle: regularity of Gaussian functionals in mean, variance and thresholds
statements.statement: Let \(d\ge1\), \(0\le r\le d\), let \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}\) have rank \(r\), and let \(\mathcal{P}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{R}_{>0}^d\times\mathbb{R}^r\) be compact. For \((m,v,u)\in\mathcal{P}\) let \(X\sim\mathcal{N}(m,\operatorname{diag}(v))\) and let \(\mathcal{E}_u:=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^d:Mx\ge-u\}\), the inequality holding coordinatewise. Then there are constants \(c_{\mathcal{P}}>0\) and \(L_{\mathcal{P}}\) such that \(\mathbb{P}[X\in\mathcal{E}_u]\ge c_{\mathcal{P}}\) on \(\mathcal{P}\), and each of the functions \[(m,v,u)\mapsto\mathbb{P}\left[X\in\mathcal{E}_u\right],\qquad\mathbb{E}\left[X_t\mathbf{1}_{X\in\mathcal{E}_u}\right],\qquad\mathbb{E}\left[X_tX_{t'}\mathbf{1}_{X\in\mathcal{E}_u}\right]\qquad(t,t'\in[d])\] is Lipschitz on \(\mathcal{P}\) with constant \(L_{\mathcal{P}}\). Consequently the conditional expectations \(\mathbb{E}[X_t\mid X\in\mathcal{E}_u]\) and \(\mathbb{E}[X_tX_{t'}\mid X\in\mathcal{E}_u]\), and the conditional covariances, are Lipschitz on \(\mathcal{P}\) as well.
statements.sectionTitle: Gaussian limits of the binomial row model
statements.moral: Gaussian probabilities and polynomial moments over moving polyhedra vary smoothly when the covariance stays nondegenerate and the boundary has zero Gaussian mass. Compact parameter sets then upgrade pointwise continuity and differentiability to the uniform bounds required by the recursion.

statements.label: lem:tilt-vs-linear-map
statements.title: Linear response to a small tilt
statements.groupTitle: linear response of the binomial row model to a small tilt (old unlabeled lemma, p. 33)
statements.statement: Fix \(\theta\in(1/2,1)\), an integer \(k\) with \(1\le k<\frac1{1-\theta}\), \(s\in\{0,1\}^k\), \(T>1\), and \(R>0\). There are constants \(\kappa=\kappa(\theta,k)>0\) and \(C=C(\theta,k,T,R)\) such that for all sufficiently large \(N\), all \(p\in(T^{-1}N^{-\theta},TN^{-\theta})\), all \(\tau\in[T^{-1},T]\), and every \(n\in\mathbb{Z}^{\{0,1\}^k}\) with \(|n[t]-\widetilde{n}[t]|\le T\sqrt N\sqrt{pN}^{\,k-1}\) for all \(t\), the following holds, where \((\widetilde n,\widetilde m,\widetilde\lambda)\) is the idealized process of Theorem 5.2 with \(D=D_\theta\) and \(\widetilde A_{s,\bullet}=A_{s,\bullet}(\widetilde n_k,\widetilde\lambda_k)\). Write \(\beta_0:=\sqrt{pN}^{\,k-1}/\sqrt N\). For \(\sigma\in\mathbb{R}^{\{0,1\}^k}\) with \(\left\lVert\sigma\right\rVert_\infty\le R\) let \(q^\sigma\in(0,1)^{\{0,1\}^k}\) be defined by \[\log\frac{q^\sigma[t]\left(n[t]-\mathbb{1}_{s=t}-p\,\widetilde n[t]\right)}{\left(1-q^\sigma[t]\right)p\,\widetilde n[t]} =\widetilde\vartheta[s,t]+\tau\beta_0\,\sigma[t],\qquad\widetilde\vartheta[s,t]:=\log\frac{\widetilde\lambda[s,t]\left(\widetilde n[t]-\mathbb{1}_{s=t}-p\,\widetilde n[t]\right)}{\left(1-\widetilde\lambda[s,t]\right)p\,\widetilde n[t]},\] and let \(A^\sigma\) have independent coordinates \(A^\sigma_t\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n[t]-\mathbb{1}_{s=t},q^\sigma[t])\). Then \(q^\sigma\) and the quantities below are smooth in \(\sigma\), \(|q^\sigma[t]-p|\le C\,p/\sqrt{pN}\), and for all \(t\in\{0,1\}^k\) and \(b\in\{0,1\}\): \(\displaystyle\left|\frac{\mathbb{E}[A^\sigma_t\mid\mathcal{I}_s(A^\sigma)]-\widetilde m[s,t]/\widetilde n[s]}{\tau\beta_0\,pN}-(\Sigma_s\sigma)[t]\right|\le CN^{-\kappa}\), where \(\Sigma_s\) is the conditional covariance of Lemma 4.6; with \(W_{s,\bullet}\) the day-\(k\) Gaussian row model, \[\begin{gathered} \left|\frac{\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{J}_{sb}(A^\sigma)\mid\mathcal{I}_s(A^\sigma)]-\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{J}_{sb}(\widetilde A_{s,\bullet})\mid\mathcal{I}_s(\widetilde A_{s,\bullet})]}{\tau\beta_0\sqrt{pN}}\right.\\ \left.-\frac{\nu[sb]}{\nu[s]}\sum_{t'}\sigma[t']\left(\mathbb{E}[W_{s,t'}\mid\mathcal{J}_{sb}(W_{s,\bullet})]-\mathbb{E}[W_{s,t'}\mid\mathcal{I}_s(W_{s,\bullet})]\right)\right|\le CN^{-\kappa}; \end{gathered}\] \(\displaystyle\left|\mathbb{E}[A^\sigma_t\mid\mathcal{J}_{sb}(A^\sigma)]-\mathbb{E}[\widetilde A_{s,t}\mid\mathcal{J}_{sb}(\widetilde A_{s,\bullet})]\right|\le C\tau\beta_0\,pN\); \(\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{I}_s(A^\sigma)]\ge\phi^\ast_k/4\) and \(\phi^\ast_k/2\le\mathbb{P}[\mathcal{J}_{sb}(A^\sigma)\mid\mathcal{I}_s(A^\sigma)]\le1-\phi^\ast_k/2\), with \(\phi^\ast_k\) the constant of Lemma 4.11.
statements.sectionTitle: The linear response of the binomial row model
statements.moral: The solving tilt is implicitly determined by conditioned row means, whose derivative is the conditional covariance. Inverting that derivative identifies the first-order tilt with \(\beta\), and differentiating the child probabilities identifies the next size response with \(\varepsilon\), uniformly over the allowed perturbations.
